explanation.text:
(Pro. 21:1-31)

rivers--irrigating channels (Psa 1:3), whose course was easily turned (compare Deu 11:10). God disposes even kings as He pleases (Pro 16:9; Psa 33:15).

bsb.text: The king’s heart is a waterway in the hand of the LORD; He directs it where He pleases.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 14:2; Pro. 16:2-25).

bsb.text: All a man’s ways seem right to him, but the LORD weighs the heart.

explanation.text: (Compare Psa 50:7-15; Isa 1:11, Isa 1:17).

bsb.text: To do righteousness and justice is more desirable to the LORD than sacrifice.

explanation.text:
high look--(Compare Margin; Psa 131:1).

proud heart--or, "heart of breadth," one that is swollen (compare Psa 101:5).

ploughing--better "lamp," a frequent figure for prosperity (Pro 20:20); hence joy or delight.

bsb.text: Haughty eyes and a proud heart—the guides of the wicked—are sin.

explanation.text: The contrast is between steady industry and rashness (compare Pro 19:2).

bsb.text: The plans of the diligent bring plenty, as surely as haste leads to poverty.

explanation.text:
The getting--or, "what is obtained" (compare Job 7:2; Jer 22:13, Hebrew).

vanity . . . to and fro--as fleeting as chaff or stubble in the wind (compare Pro 20:17-21; Psa 62:10). Such gettings are unsatisfactory.

them . . . death--act as if they did (Pro 8:36; Pro 17:19).

bsb.text: Making a fortune by a lying tongue is a vanishing mist, a deadly pursuit.

explanation.text:
robbery--or, "destruction," especially oppression, of which they are authors.

shall destroy--literally, "cut with a saw" (Kg1 7:9), that is, utterly ruin them. Their sins shall be visited on them in kind.

to do judgment--what is just and right.

bsb.text: The violence of the wicked will sweep them away because they refuse to do what is just.

explanation.text: of man--any one; his way is opposed to truth, and also estranged from it. The pure proves himself such by his right conduct.

bsb.text: The way of a guilty man is crooked, but the conduct of the innocent is upright.

explanation.text:
corner--a turret or arbor on the roof.

brawling--or contentious.

wide house--literally, "house of fellowship," large enough for several families.

bsb.text: Better to live on a corner of the roof than to share a house with a quarrelsome wife.

explanation.text: So strongly does he desire to do evil (Psa 10:3; Ecc 8:11), that he will not even spare his friend if in his way.

bsb.text: The soul of the wicked man craves evil; his neighbor finds no favor in his eyes.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 19:25). That which the simple learn by the terrors of punishment, the wise learn by teaching.

bsb.text: When a mocker is punished, the simple gain wisdom; and when a wise man is instructed, he acquires knowledge.

explanation.text:
(Compare Psa 37:35-38; Psa 73:17, Psa 73:20).

house--family or interests.

overthroweth--either supply "God" (compare Pro 10:24), or the word is used impersonally.

bsb.text: The Righteous One considers the house of the wicked and brings the wicked to ruin.

explanation.text: The principles of retribution, often taught (compare Psa 18:26; Mat 7:1-12).

bsb.text: Whoever shuts his ears to the cry of the poor, he too shall cry out and receive no answer.

explanation.text: The effect of bribery (Pro 17:23) is enhanced by secrecy, as the bribed person does not wish his motives made known.

bsb.text: A gift in secret soothes anger, and a covert bribe pacifies great wrath.

explanation.text: But the just love right and need no bribes. The wicked at last meet destruction, though for a time happy in concealing corruption.

bsb.text: Justice executed is a joy to the righteous, but a terror to the workers of iniquity.

explanation.text:
the way of understanding--(Compare Pro 12:26; Pro 14:22).

remain--that is, rest as at a journey's end; death will be his unchanging home.

bsb.text: The man who strays from the path of understanding will rest in the assembly of the dead.

explanation.text: Costly luxuries impoverish.

bsb.text: He who loves pleasure will become poor; the one who loves wine and oil will never be rich.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 11:8). By suffering what they had devised for the righteous, or brought on them, the wicked became their ransom, in the usual sense of substitutes (compare Jos 7:26; Est 7:9).

bsb.text: The wicked become a ransom for the righteous, and the faithless for the upright.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 21:9).

wilderness--pasture, though uninhabitable ground (Psa 65:12).

bsb.text: Better to live in the desert than with a contentious and ill-tempered wife.

explanation.text:
The wise, by diligence and care, lay up and increase wealth, while fools

spend--literally, "swallow it up," greedily.

bsb.text: Precious treasures and oil are in the dwelling of the wise, but a foolish man consumes them.

explanation.text: He who tries to act justly and kindly (Psa 34:14) will prosper and obtain justice and honor.

bsb.text: He who pursues righteousness and loving devotion finds life, righteousness, and honor.

explanation.text:
"Wisdom is better than strength" (Ecc 7:19; Ecc 9:15).

strength . . . thereof--that in which they confide.

bsb.text: A wise man scales the city of the mighty and pulls down the stronghold in which they trust.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 13:2-3; Jam 3:6-10).

bsb.text: He who guards his mouth and tongue keeps his soul from distress.

explanation.text: The reproachful name is deserved by those who treat others with anger and contempt.

bsb.text: Mocker is the name of the proud and arrogant man—of him who acts with excessive pride.

explanation.text: desire--that is, of ease and idleness brings him to starvation.

bsb.text: The craving of the slacker kills him because his hands refuse to work.

explanation.text: The sin of covetousness marks the sluggard, as the virtue of benevolence the righteous.

bsb.text: All day long he covets more, but the righteous give without restraint.

explanation.text:
God regards the heart, and hypocrisy is more odious than open inconsistency.

wicked mind--or, "design" (Pro 1:4).

bsb.text: The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable—how much more so when brought with ill intent!

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 19:5).

that heareth--or heeds instruction, and so grows wise.

speaketh constantly--or sincerely (compare Hab 1:5), and hence is believed (Pro 12:19; Jam 1:19).

bsb.text: A lying witness will perish, but the man who listens to truth will speak forever.

explanation.text:
hardeneth his face--is obstinate.

directeth . . . way--considers it, and acts advisedly.

bsb.text: A wicked man hardens his face, but the upright man makes his way sure.

explanation.text:
Men's best devices and reliances are vain compared with God's, or without His aid (Pro 19:21; Psa 20:7; Psa 33:17).

Next: Proverbs Chapter 22

bsb.text: There is no wisdom, no understanding, no counsel that can prevail against the LORD.

explanation.text:
The horse is prepared against the day of battle,.... The horse is a warlike creature, and was much used formerly, as now, in war; these are prepared against the day of battle, to mount the cavalry with; and men are apt to put too great confidence in them: this is mentioned instead of all other military preparations and instruments of war;

but safety is of the Lord; a horse is a vain thing for safety, Psalm 33:17; victory is only of the Lord; salvation depends upon him; it is he that covers men's heads in the day of battle, and gives them victory over their enemies: or "salvation is of the Lord"; this is true of spiritual and eternal salvation, as well as of temporal salvation; it is of the Lord, Father, Son and Spirit; and so is the safety of the saints; and their final perseverance to eternal glory, which is owing to the love of God, covenant interest, security in Christ, the grace of the Spirit, and the power of God; see Hosea 14:3.

bsb.text: A horse is prepared for the day of battle, but victory is of the LORD.
